Republic ofthe Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 14 July 2008 ND 55 —S. 200S...--E MR. ADONIS H. REBADULIA Sangguniang Panlalawigan Secretary Provincial Capitol Building Catarman, Nor hern Samar Dear Mr. Rebadulia: This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal opinion on ' this aforequoted query: "Whether or not the resignation of the Honorable Alfredo S. Dulay, Sr. has become effective and operative, and that he is considered resigned as member of the Sangguniang panlalawigan of Northern Samar?" Per your letter and other attached documents submitted to this Office, the following are the antecedent facts, viz: 'a Mr. Alfredo S. Dulay, SY. was elected as Member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, that Province, during the May 2007 Synchronized National and Local Elections; a ' On 07 December 2007, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Northern Samar unanimously adopted Sangguniang Panlalawigan Resolution No. 59, series of 2007, entitled "Resolution Recommending Madame Carmen A. Dulay as Replacement of the Honorable Alfredo S. Dulay, Sr. in the Event his Position as Member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Northern Samar is Rendered Permanently Vacant"; 'a On 14 January 2008, SP Member Dulay delivered a privilege speech during the session of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in which he announced his intended resignation due to health reason; On 21 January 2008, SP Member Dulay tendered a letter Of resignation to Vice-Governor Antonio P. Lucero, his resignation made effective 21 January 2008; On 22 January 2008, Vice-Governor Antonio P. Lucero accepted SP Member Dulay's resignation effective at the close of office hours on 21 January 2008;

On 28 January 2008, SP Member Dulay attended the session of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and delivered a speech to withdraw his letter of reSignation; In the same session, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan unanimously granted the request of SP Member Dulay to withdraw his earlier tendered resignation; On 13 February 2008, Governor Raul Daza wrote a Memorandum to Vice- Governor Lucero and the Members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan expressing his view that the resignation of SP Member Dulay has become *effective at the close of the office hours on 21 January 2008 and that the withdrawal kly him of his letter of resi ation on 28 January 2008 has no leg'ål effect; p On 26 February 2008, Vice-Governor Lucero, in reply to the Memorandum, opined that the resignation of SP Member Dulay on 21 Jariuary 2008 has , never been completed and therefore never became effective as it was promptly withdrawn by him on 28 January 2008. Hence, your query. In reply tnereto, we answer in the negative. Please allow us to illustrate how we arrived to this conclusion. In the case of Ortiz uS. COMELEC (162 SCRA 812), the Supreme Court defined resignation as the "act of giving up or the act of an officer by Which he declines his office and renounces the further right to use it. It is an expression of the incumbent in some form, yxpress or implied, of the intention to surrender, renounce, and relinquish the office and the acceptance by competent and lawful guthority". •In the case of Sangguniang Bayan of San Andres, Catanduanes vs. Court Of Appeals (G.R. No. 11883, 16 January 1998), the Supreme Court held that to constitute a complete and operative resignation from public Office, there must be: (a) an intention to relinquish a part of the term; (b) an 'act of relinquishment; and (c) an acceptance by the proper authority. Moreover, in Punzalan uS. Mendoza (140 SCRA 153), the Court held implicitly, but no less clearly, that the effectivity of a public official's resignation depends not on such much on its terms, e.g. "effective at the p Of the President", or "at a particular time or on the bappening of a particular contingency, but as a legal proposition, on acceptance thereof by the proper authority. For quite obviously, such appropriate authority can disregard the terms of the .. (cited in official's resignation, and as easily reject it as accept It . ' ' Joson vs. Nario 187 SCRA 453). cceptance by the proper authority is required by reason of Article 238 of the Revised Penal Code, which makes abandonment of office crimi-

nally punishable. To be a valid resignation, the tender thereof must be in yvriting and must be accepted by the public officer authorized by law to accept the same. After having discussed the principles of tender of resignation and its ecceptance, may we now proceed to the pertinent provisions of the Local overnment de with r,espect to resignation of Sanggunian members. Section 2 of the Local Government Code provides and we quote: "SECTION 82. Resignation of Elective Local OfficiaZ9.-(a) Resignation by elective Zocai officials shall be deemed e ective onl u on acce tance b the following authorities: 1) T e President, in the case Of governor, Vice governors, and mayors and vice mayors of highly urbaniz€d cities and independent component cities; 2) The governor, in the case of municipal mayors, municipal vice-mayors, city mayors and city vice- mayors of component cities 3) The san unian concerned in the case o sanggunian members; and 4) The city or municipal mayor, • in the case of barangty officials. (b) Copies of the resignation letters of elective local officials, together with the action taken. by the aforementioned authorities, shall be furnished the Department of the Interior and Local Government. (C) The resignation shall be deemed accepted if not acted upon by the authority concerned within fifteen (15) working days from receipt thereof. (d) Irrevocable resignations by sanggunian members shall be deemed acce ted u on resentation before an open session of the sanggunian concerned and duly entered in its records: provided, however, That this subsection does not apply to sanggunian members who are subject to recall elections or to cases where existing laws prescribe the manner of acting upon such resignation." (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the aforequoted Section 82 (a)(3), resignation by Spngguniang • Panlalawigan Members shall be deemed effective only upon acceptance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan concerned. It is the therefore, that per Section 82 (a)(3) of the Code, obvious, Sangguniang Panlalawigan is the body vested by law with the authority to

accept resignation •tendered by its members so that the acceptance of the •resignation has to be decided by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as a collegial body. In the case of SP Member Dulay, may it be noted that while he indeed tendered his letter of resignation to Vice-Governor Lucero, the acceptance made by the latter, however, is not the legal acceptance contemplated under the law because Vice-Governor Lucero alone is not the Sanggunian authorized by law to accept the same. The acceptance should have been made by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as a collegial body. One may argue, however, that what is applicable to SP Member Dulay's resignation is Section 82 (d) of the Local Government Code pertaining to irrevocable resignation by sanggunian members presented before an open session of the sangguniang concerned. We are not convinced. With respect to Section 82 (d), irrevocable resignation by Sanggunian members shall be deemed accepted upon presentation before an open session of the Sanggunian concerned and duly entered in its records. Unlike the previously discussed resignation contemplated under Section 82 (a)(3) ot the Local Government Code, the resignation being irrevocable under Section 82 (d), by operation of law, it is deemed accepted by •the Sanggunian upon presentation before an open session and duly entered in its records. With respect to the case of SP Member Dulay, he merely announced his intended resignation in an open session on 14 January 2008. Let it be noted that Section 82 (d) of the Code requires that the resignation should be categorically denominated as irrevocable so that it shall be deemed accepted, by operation of law, once presented before an open session Of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. A reading of the attached copy of the privilege speech delivered by SP Member Dulay would reveal that it failed to expressly mention the word "irrevocable" pertaining to his intended resignation. AS such, it is therefore incumbent upon us to determine whether the irrevocable nature of the resignation made by SP Member Dulay can be deduced from the tenor of the privilege speech delivered. Ordinarily, the term "irrevocable" means 'final or irreversible". In the Webster's 3rd New International Dictionary, the term "irrevocable" implies that which is "incapable of being recalled or revoked" and the term "irrevocably" implies that which is "beyond any possibility of change" (p. 1196). We are of the view that the tenor of the privilege speech is not persuasive of any irrevocability. Undeniably, the privilege speech delivered by SP Member Dulay captured his sadness in leaving- his post. He said that he delivered his speech with a heavy heart and his decision to resign was a difficult one. He even consulted some of his trusted friends for some insights regarding his resignation and, in fact, he was convinced that resignation is not an option. If only he is physically capacitated to do so, he will not leave his post. Here, we can reasonably deduce that SP

-5- Member Dulay was in doubt in leaving his post. In this connection, the case of Gamboa uS. Court Of Appeals, 108 SCRA 1, is instructive. The Supreme Court held in this case that "To constitute a complete and operative resignation of public office there must be an intention to relinquish a part of the term, accompanied by the act of relinquishment and a resignation implies an expression of the incumbent in some form. express or implied. of the intention to surrender, renounce, and relinquish the office and the acceptance by competent and lawful authority". Thus, we can say that in rendering the privilege speech, SP Member Dulay simply manifested his intention to resign. Precisely, to operationalize such intention, he tendered a formal letter of resignation to Vice Governor Lucero on 21 January 2008. In the case of Joson uS. Nario (187 SCRA 453, 13 July 1990), the Supreme Court had the occasion to consider that the decided weight of authority is that "apart from legat provision, xx the mere presentation of resignation does not work a vacancy, and a resignation is not complete until accepted by proper authority" (McQuillin, E., The Law of Municipal Corporations, 3rd Ed., 1949, Voi. 3, p. 443) and "x x until acceptance by proper authority, the tender or offer to resign is revocable", unless otherwise provided by statute" (Dillon, JF., Commentaries on the Law of Municipal Corporations, Voi. 1, pp. 723, 1911). This is not to say that a public officer may not resign. Mechem says that he " 'may certainly resign, but without acceptance his resignation is nothing, and he remains in office. He is, therefore, so far as the rights of third persons are concerned, not only still clothed with authority, but is subject to the burdens of the office and he may be compelled to perform the duties, and is liable for their non-performance, as before" [Mechem, Treatise on the Law Of Public Offices and Officers(1889), 263-264, citing Chief Justice Ruffin]. Foregoing considered, there being procedural infirmities in the tender and acceptance of SP Dulay's resignation, we believe that he cannot as yet be considered to have effectively resigned trom nis Office. At this juncture, it may be well to note the arguments embodied in the Comment tiled by Governor Raul A. Daza dated 29 May 2008, which was received by the Department on 02 June 2008. Governor Daza confirmed all our abovestated antecedent facts, except that in Paragraph 3 thereof, it was . erroneously indicated that SP Resolution No. 59, series of 2008 was unanimously passed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Northern Samar on 17 December 2007, instead of 07 December 2007. Governor Daza prayed that the Department confirms the resignation of SP Member Dulay and in support thereto, he averred the following arguments, which we quoted in whole and in part, to wit: (a) The intention of Mr. Dulay to resign as member of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of N orthern Samar is indeed unmistakabie. Because it was accompanied by an actual act of relinquishment, his resignation was effective and operative. His

resignation was both oral and written. More than implied, it was express; (b) Moreover, there is no question that he tendered his resignation to, and it was accepted by, the Sanggunian Panlalawigan through its Presiding Officer, Vice-Governor Lucero, pursuant to Section 82 of the par. a (3) and d of the Local Government Code xxx; iAThen Mr. Dulay presented his resignation in open session, indisputably, he tendered the same to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan as a collegial body; (d) In compliance with the above-cited provision of the law, all the events taken together, especially those that occurred during the sessions, could only show that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan was "deemed" to have accepted Mr. Dulay's resignation. Moreover, his letter to the Vice-Governor was an emphatic reiteration of his resignation to the Presiding Officer, who represented and symbolized the Sanggunian as a collective body. Conversely, when the Vice-Governor signed the letter of acceptance he likewise represented and symbolized the Sanggunian as a collective body; and in fine, the totality of events surrounding the issue resoundingly speaks that it was an effective and operative resignation which rendered Mr. Dulay's position vacant.' In this regard, even assuming, without admitting, that based on the arguments of Governor Daza, SP Member Dulay has already effectively resigned from office, the action made by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan on 28 January 2008 is, however, very material and vital. Let it be noted that in the factual antecedents, which you yourself narrated in the subject letter and in other attached documents submitted to the Department, you categorically stated that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan unanimously granted on 28 January 2008 the request of SP Member Dulay to withdraw his earlier tendered resignation. In this regard, the ratiocination made by the Supreme Court in the case of Rubio, ur. y—. Sto. Tomas (183 SCRA 571) pertaining to withdrawal of resignation is instructive. The Supreme Court ruled therein that an immediately effective resignation may be withdrawn before it is acted upon, but not after acceptance. It has also been held that a resignation of an officer, effective at a future date, may not be withdrawn after the resignation has been accepted. Accordingly, a public employee is entitled to withdraw a prospective resignation it the employee does so before its effective date, before it has been accepted, and before the appointing power acts in reliance of the resignation. Along this line, an officer may withdraw his resignation at _any time before it is accepted. and after it has been make the withdrawal by the consent of the authorjw

accepting, where no new rights have intervened (Mechém, supra, 265 as cited in De Leon and De Leon, Jr., The Law on Public Officers and Election Law, 3rd Ed. 1997, p. 324). Since the Sangguniang Panlalawigan unanimously granted SP Member Dulay's withdrawal of his earlier resignation, which is therefore the consent of the accepting authority, SP Dulay's resignation is considered legally withdrawn. Harmonizing now the law and the facts involved, we are of the humble view that the issue on whether or not SP Member Dulay's resignation has become effective and operative is already rendered moot and academic when the Sangguniang Panlungsod has unanimously granted on 28 January 2008 the request of SP Member Dulay to withdraw his earlier tendered resignation. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE 0/ Undersecretary l/ Legal: 17 Hon. Rapl Daza cc: Provincial Capitol Northern Samar Director William C. Paler DILG Regional Office No. 08 Tacloban City
